newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shares mixed ahead of rates decision.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shares mixed ahead of rates decision.

text.p: Israeli shares closed mixed with a negative bias on Sunday in very thin trading ahead of a Bank of Israel interest rate announcement on Monday, traders said.

The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares lost 0.23 percent, or 0.44 points, to 188.03 on very low turnover of 37 million shekels against 39 million on Thursday, the last day of trading before the Israeli weekend.
The Maof 25 blue chip index fell 0.22 percent to 198.45.
"The market is stuck and investors are sitting on the fence waiting for the interest rate announcement on Monday," said Ronen Kaufman at Nesuah Trading and Investments.

In its weekly report First International Bank said the Bank of Israel is expected to lower the interest rate by 0.5 percentage points. The central bank will announce interest rates for November on Monday. The key short-term rate is now 15.5 percent.

"Activity was minimal today and there were no players in the market. The only thing that can move the market now is the dollar. A devaluation of the shekel would spark the market," said Elisha Rosenfeld at Lehava Securities.

Kaufman said he was optimsitic that would happen. "Despite the low activity, the market will soon start rising again. The lowering of the interest rate, the declining shekel and the slowing economy will lead eventually to an improvement in the stock market," he said.

Tadiran, the third most active share, surged 4.25 percent to 1,367 on volume of 1.3 million shekels after its New York-traded share rose 4.5 percent on Thursday. Tadiran traded quietly in New York on Friday.

The most active shares were Koor Industries, which fell 0.75 percent to 28,900 on turnover of 1.7 million shekels, and Teva Pharmaceutical Industries, which lost 1.5 percent to 136,554 on turnover of 1.6 million shekels.
